items.quote: As far as India story is concerned is, as we say, it's an India story. It's an India story is about emerging market story, which should be seen in its own merit and its own isolated effect.

items.statement: Energy transition investments in renewable generation, green corridors, EV charging, green hydrogen driving demand for ABB's portfolio
items.quote: We have actually tabulated renewable energy generation, green energy corridor, EV and charging infrastructure, and green hydrogen and certain data, that's how we read in the marketplace.

items.statement: Material cost advantage from commodity timing difference will thin down as prices stabilize
items.quote: But I think now that the prices are stabilizing at this point of time as what we see, that particular difference between the order booking to the execution time advantages will start to thin down going forward.

items.statement: New Group CEO Morten Wierod (from Aug 1) has growth mandate while maintaining profitability; familiar with India as former Chairman
items.quote: Now given that we have our colleague, Morten Wierod who has taken over a CEO from 1st of August, and he was, by the way, also Chairman of ABB in India. He frequents India very well. He knows India very well.

items.statement: Order booking guidance for FY25 is Rs 20,000-22,000 crore
items.quote: Now, w hen you come to the guidance , w e have given a guidance for order booking in the range of Rs. 20,000-Rs. 22,000 crores for FY24-25

items.statement: Invoice booking growth guidance for FY25 is 15%
items.quote: We have given a guidance of 15% growth in invoice booking against which in 1st Quarter, we achieved 23% despite the elections and steep high temperatures at various

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is 9.5-10%, confident of achieving at least 9.5%
items.quote: With respect to the margins , the Company achieved 9.3% EBITDA margin in Q1 as against guidance given for the range of 9.5 %-10% for the year as a w hole. So, going forw ard, we expect to reach 9.5% EBITDA margins

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 52,626 crore at end of June 2024 after Rs 408 crore inflow in Q1
items.quote: And the order book position as on the beginning of the year, the order book was Rs. 57,536 crores and we have received an order of Rs. 408 crores in the 1st Quarter. After eliminating the exhibition in the 1st Quarter, the order book stands at Rs. 52,626 crores as at the end of June '24.

items.statement: L1 orders worth ~Rs 8,700 crore pending (two MSRDC and one other project)
items.quote: And sir, L1 orders are two MSRDC and one another project or the values are close to Rs. 8,700 odd crores, if you can reconfirm? Sanjay Pusarla: About that number only, yes.

items.statement: Rs 8,500 crore of orders in pipeline expected to mature in Q2 FY25
items.quote: One is that we have already explained you earlier that about Rs. 8,500 crores are the orders which are in the pipeline and we are expecting those orders to get matured maybe in this quarter.

items.statement: Prospective project pipeline of ~Rs 2,00,000 crore for next 12-15 months
items.quote: Mr. Kapoor, we have a very healthy prospective pipeline of projects close to Rs. 2,00,000 crore. It is a prospective pipeline of projects, but it depends at what ti me client intends to award which project

items.statement: Positive outlook for Andhra Pradesh projects after government change; Rs 5,000 crore of abandoned Capital City orders may restart
items.quote: So, therefore, lot of discussions takes place between the client and the NCC. And basing o n the conclusions, so roughly at this moment we can say about Rs. 5,000 crores those orders may restart

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission: 60% complete by June 2024, Rs 6,000 crore balance, target 95% completion by March 2025
items.quote: About the Jal Jeevan projects, by end of June '24 we have completed 60% of the projects. And the balance we have about Rs. 6,000 crores as on this date and by March 2025, we expect to complete about 95% of these projects.

items.statement: Smart Meter Bihar: 80,000 meters supplied, 55,000 installed; Maharashtra progress slow due to election uncertainty
items.quote: About the Smart Meter projects , Bihar project is one already we issued the orders for suppl y for meters and supplied the meters , about 80,000 meters supplied and 55,000 meters we installed and also the software system is also installed into that one

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 9.33%; confident of achieving guided 9.5% for full year
items.quote: Yes, in the guidance, what we given 9.5%-10% the range we have given, so the 1st Quarter we achieved about 9.33%. So, as a result at this moment, the minimum range band whatever is there 9.5%, we are confident to achieve 9.5% level.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget Rs 250 crore; Rs 51 crore spent in Q1 (excludes J Kumar JV TBM)
items.quote: Full year, we were budgeting around Rs. 250 crores and we have done around Rs. 51 crores at the end of the 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Trade receivables Rs 3,654 crore (86 days) at June 2024 vs Rs 3,063 crore (82 days) year ago; Rs ~500 crore collected in July 2024
items.quote: The debtors stand at Rs. 3,654 crores as against Rs. 3,063 crores as on same date of the previous year and compared to the 31st March, it was almost like Rs. 900 crores higher when compared to 31st March.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue Rs 4,719 crore (25% of turnover) at June 2024 vs Rs 3,859 crore at March 2024; cleared in July
items.quote: Unbilled revenue as on 30th June is Rs. 4,719 crores as against Rs. 3,859 crores in the March ‘24 which is 25% of the turnover . When compared to the previous year , previous year it was 21% and this year i t was

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 1,819 crore at June 2024 (up Rs 814 crore from March); target Rs 500 crore by end FY25
items.quote: So, now according to our plan is to stand at Rs. 500 crores debt level by end of FY25.

items.statement: Finance cost reduced to 3.25% (gross) and 2.8% (net) in Q1 FY25 from 3.45% and 3.03% year ago
items.quote: The finance cost when we compared with the last year, the finance costs have come down from 3.45% to 3.25%. The gross finance cost is Rs. 153 crores and the net finance costs after eliminating the income and in terms of interest is coming to Rs. 132 crores, which is 2.8% in the 1st Quarter of this year.

items.statement: Average interest rate on interest-bearing advances (72% of Rs 2,425 crore) down to 9.5% from 9.72% at March 2024
items.quote: And the average interest works out to 9.5%, which is less than what it was there as on March '24 which is 9.72% and a year before, it was 10.72%.

items.statement: TAQA settlement: Rs 45 crore second installment paid in June; third installment due December
items.quote: We have paid the second installment of Rs. 45 crores. Sanjay Pusarla: Rs. 45 crores which is due in June and the third last installment, is due in December and we expect to pay on time as scheduled.

items.statement: Board approved amalgamation of wholly-owned subsidiary NCC Infrastructure Holdings for tax benefits and administrative simplification
items.quote: NCCIHL is a wholly owned subsidiary. That is the reason we thought okay, we will merge that into this. Two things which we were thinking to achieve, one is on the tax benefits by getting the dividends into the main Company.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh receivables: Rs 150 crore Capital City + Rs 350-400 crore running projects; expect Rs 300 crore in weeks
items.quote: The first part is about the funds blocked on account of the Capital City projects are about Rs. 150 crores. And the running projects are about Rs. 350 or Rs. 400 crores are there. So, now, already the dialogues are taking place with the government and we expect nearly Rs. 300 crores to materialize in couple of weeks out of that one.

items.statement: Vizag Urban: Rs 67.25 crore received in Q1; balance Rs 33 crore equity expected in 2-3 months; Rs 377 crore loan over 2 years
items.quote: in t he 1st Quarter we received an amount of Rs. 67.25 crores relating to the sale of our equity investment and a balance investment of Rs. 33 crores we expect to receive in 2-3 months period

items.statement: O&M revenue ~4-5% of major order book; Rs 400-500 crore in current revenue
items.quote: From the O&M content, we can take about 4%-5% of the major order book will be there. Saket Kapoor: So, the revenue of Rs. 5,500 crore has O&M component of Rs. 550 crore to be precise? R. S. Raju: Yes Rs. 400-Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission execution ~Rs 1,200-1,600 crore per quarter; Rs 1,212 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: To answer your question, how much have we done in the 1st Quarter Rs. 1,212, I repeat what we have done in the 1st Quarter is Rs. 1,212 crores.

items.statement: Maharashtra Smart Meter progress slow in Q2-Q3 due to election uncertainty; pickup expected in Q4
items.quote: So, thereby we expect that Q2 and Q3 may not be there good progress and in Q4, we expect to pick up the progress on that run.

items.statement: Selective bidding approach maintained; ERM committee reviews state/vertical risk; no aggressive bidding in AP despite positive outlook
items.quote: Being a listed Company, we have a committee of the Board ERM and we look at the state wise , vertical wise risk very carefully. So, not only for the AP , for any state or any vertical for that matter, we do n ot really believe in going aggressively, just bidding for the sake of bidding

items.statement: Expects Yarn division outlook to improve in Q2 and further in Q3-Q4; Fabric strong throughout; Garment to pick up significantly in Q3-Q4; not a disastrous year, sees inflection point
items.quote: So, I think that the outlook for the Yarn division in Quarter 2 will be better and Quarter 3, Quarter 4 will be even better. So, that's as far as the Yarn division is concerned. Fabric, it looks wonderful all throughout. And Garment will start to pick up also in Quarter 3, Quarter 4 in significant ways.

items.statement: Expects finance cost around Rs. 35 crores for FY25, changing quarter-on-quarter due to CAPEX
items.quote: It will be in the range of around Rs. 35 crores but let's see how we go ahead on the CAPEX and how do we increas e. So, it will be changing quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Estimated CAPEX of Rs. 180-190 crores over 18-24 months for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So, expected CAPEX over a period of 2 years, if I can draw the line of sight then it will be in the range of around Rs. 180 crores to Rs. 190 crores, but it will be over a period of 18 to 24 months, not all at a time.

items.statement: Seeing demand recovery in H2 FY25 from Western markets including Eastern Europe
items.quote: Yes, we are seeing recovery in the second half of the year in demand from all markets in the West. It has been bad earlier, but now it seems to be improving quite well.

items.statement: Domestic formal wear pipeline empty, big wedding season ahead driving jacket demand
items.quote: by and large, the demand for jackets now seems to be on an upward trend, primarily because the pipeline for Indian domestic formal wear is quite empty and we see a big wedding season ahead.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to ~61% in Q1 FY25 from 56-57% earlier despite higher raw material costs, due to value-added products
items.quote: if you look at overall gross margin, and you compare our gross margin this quarter versus our gross margin last quarter or even over the previous financial year gross margin average to the gross margin in this quarter, this quarter is better with about 60 point some percent, 61% almost gross margin, whereas earlier, the gross margin w as like 56%, 57%.

items.statement: Simone brand has Rs. 25 crores bookings for FY25, targets Rs. 500-1000 crores in 5-6 years
items.quote: We have bookings of Rs. 25 crores already for this financial year in Simone. And we expect this brand to grow to really be a sizable brand in the coming years.

items.statement: Uniform business with Eastern European armies (Czechoslovakian, Slovakian) and working on Dutch, German uniforms
items.quote: you have seen that we have engaged with several diffe rent armies in Eastern Europe like we have the business from the Czechoslovakian Army, the Slovakian Army. We are working on the Dutch uniforms and the German uniforms.

items.statement: Targets Fabric utilization back to 80-85% by end of FY25; Garment to 60-80% by Q3-Q4
items.quote: we should be by the end of the year at back to 80%, 85% utilization as far as Fabric is concerned. Garment is the one which was the concerning one where we actually went down to almost 45% utilization. And we should try and get back there to the 60, 70s, 80s by Quarter 3, Quarter 4.

items.statement: Increasing external yarn sourcing (cotton, filament polyester, Chinese poly viscose) for Fabric business; internal yarn usage percentage to decline
items.quote: On regular yarns like filament yarns etc., we are sourcing more. And the percentage of fabric that we are producing based on cotton yarn that we buy from outside and filament polyester that we buy from outside is increasing. We are even importing certain Chinese poly viscose specialty yarns.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest may benefit India long-term but not immediately; duty advantage for Bangladesh remains a barrier; Vietnam dominates knitwear
items.quote: Long term, yes, if customers have been rattled once and now are putting a question mark on the political stability in Bangladesh, long term, they will look towards India. So, we do expect benefits to happen down the road. Immediately, maybe it won't be such a big impact.

items.statement: Seeing good export demand from Eastern European countries (Poland, Czechoslovakia, Slovakia); uniform business with Eastern European armies
items.quote: we are seeing a lot of demand even in Europe, particularly from the Eastern European countries like Poland, Czechoslovakia, Slovakia and all of the countries, we are seeing a good demand.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory increased slightly in Q1 due to pipeline orders; raw material inventory stable; will be billed in subsequent period
items.quote: Yes, there is a little in this quarter, the inventory on finished goods has little been increased. But that is all because of the orders what we have in pipeline. So, it will get billed in a subsequent period.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings increasing due to CAPEX plan; finance cost expected around Rs. 35 crores in FY25
items.quote: we are looking for a CAPEX plan in our worsted and we are also looking for decongesting our mill and making some realignment. So, we are doing some civil work and all that. So, there will be addition in our long -term borrowings.

items.statement: Total income declined 10% YoY to Rs. 274.7 crores; EBITDA Rs. 20.8 crores; PAT Rs. 1 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our total income declined by 10% to Rs. 274.7 crores in Q1 FY '25 on a year-on-year basis. The EBITDA stood at Rs. 20.8 crores during the 1st Quarter. Profit before depreciation tax came in at Rs. 12.7 crores and the company recorded a PAT of Rs. 1 crore in the 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Tesca technical textiles turnover Rs. 19 crores in Q1; flat QoQ, down 16% YoY; defense technical textiles growing
items.quote: For Tesca Quarter 1, we did a turnover of about Rs. 19 crores. And our quarter-on-quarter growth seems to be flat, but the year-on-year sort of declined by about 16%. However, this again looks pretty good for Quarter 2, Quarter 3.

items.statement: Labor shortages during election season impacted Yarn division volumes in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The decline is attributed to the muted demand along with labor shortages due to the election season.

items.statement: This is the worst quarter in a long time; expects everything to be better from here onwards
items.quote: We do recognize that this has been the worst quarter that we have experienced in a long time in terms of the financial results. However, this is as bad as it gets. And we expect everything to be better from here onwards.

items.statement: Management cannot forecast future quarterly performance or simulate Q1 to Q4 trends
items.quote: From Q1 to Q4 last year, what you saw, whether you can use that as a yardstick to project you into Q4 this year. Unfortunately, my capabilities and knowledge do not lie in that area, I'm not able to help you there.

items.statement: Registered investors grew 51% from 12.1 crore to 18.4 crore UCC
items.quote: When I joined BSE, registered investors based on Unique Client Code UCC, stood at INR 12.1 crores, which has increased to INR 18.4 crores as on date, a growth of 51%.

items.statement: Cash segment average daily turnover more than doubled to INR 9,006 crores
items.quote: BSE's average daily turnover in the cash segment for Q1 FY 2025 stands at INR 9,006 crores as compared to INR 4,025 crores in the same quarter last year on account of a buoyant market.

items.statement: Sensex derivatives hit record 54 crore contracts traded with notional turnover of INR 432 lakh crores
items.quote: It also gives me great pleasure to inform you that Sensex derivatives continues to grow and broke its record on 26 July 2024, at more than 54 crores contracts traded representing a notional turnover of INR 432 lakh crores.

items.statement: Bankex derivatives hit record 25.9 crore contracts traded with notional turnover of INR 230 lakh crores
items.quote: The Bankex contracts have also generated significant interest since its expiry date changed to Monday from October 16, 2023, by creating a new record on 29th July 2024, with 25.9 crores contract traded representing a notional turnover of INR 230 lakh crores.

items.statement: Single stock derivatives launched July 2024 with 155 members in futures and 35 in options
items.quote: BSE forayed into single stock derivatives space with effect from 1st July 2024, with a mid-month expiry for the second Thursday of the month. So far, 155 members have participated in single stock futures and 35 single stock options.

items.statement: Net profit attributable to shareholders INR 265 crores up 253% YoY excluding CDSL stake sale
items.quote: The net profit attributable to shareholders as the company stands at INR 265 crores, up from INR 75.1 crores, excluding CDSL Stake Sale, a growth of 253%.

items.statement: Redesigning derivatives charge structure to uniform per-unit pricing per SEBI 'true to label' circular
items.quote: BSE is also in the process of redesigning the existing charge structure which will be uniform for all the members in the equity derivatives segment to confirm the SEBI circular stating the market infrastructure institutions have to be true to label.

items.statement: Regulatory charge INR 1,200 per crore, clearing and settlement charge INR 1,200-1,300 per crore on premium turnover
items.quote: See around INR 1,200 crores to INR 1,300 per crores, INR 1,200 crores is the regulatory charge. That is very clear. INR 1,300 to INR 1,200 is the clearing and settlement charges that we pay.

items.statement: SEBI consultation papers on derivatives framework, interest income on collateral, and MII charges under review; feedback deadline August 20, 2024
items.quote: SEBI has constituted the expert working group on the topic, which you mentioned about derivatives, which confabulated and gave their thoughts to the regulators which was discussed in committee called Secondary Markets Advisory Committee and the public consultation paper has been published by SEBI, requesting for views from the market till August 20, 2024.

items.statement: No regulatory target set for F&O SGF contribution yet; regulator reviewing adequacy based on risk analysis
items.quote: I would like to clarify to you that we do not, at this point of time, have any regulatory targets stipulated to us in terms of SGF requirement, from F&O. That is a first clarification.

items.statement: Treasury income on clearing funds INR 62 crores; only excess unutilized collateral may need interest pass-through per consultation paper
items.quote: The total number is INR 62 crores, which is coming out of the treasury income of ICCL. That is the number I can say.

items.statement: Submitted representations to SEBI on turnover fee matter; awaiting response, provision already made in prior quarter
items.quote: We always do what we promise to do and keeping up our promise, we have had detailed discussions and we have submitted our submissions to the kind review of the regulators.

items.statement: Investing in StAR MF scalability and functionality; launching StAR MF 2.0 this quarter
items.quote: Given the growth, we are going to continue investing in StAR MF and improve it in terms of scalability, functionality, order processing and introduce a new platform called StAR MF 2.0 this quarter.

items.statement: 430+ members trading BSE derivatives representing 47 lakh active clients since relaunch
items.quote: Since relaunch, more than 430 members have traded the BSE derivatives representing around 47 lakh active clients.

items.statement: Currency segment SGF surplus exists; reversal requires regulatory discussion
items.quote: The fact that the regulatory -- the earlier regulatory clarification has resulted in not being any volumes in currency segment, and therefore, the need for the settlement guarantee fund coming down is well known and highly appreciated. But to take back that money and reuse it elsewhere as part of settlement guarantee fund would require regulatory discussions.

items.statement: Regulatory changes may impact derivatives volumes but also create new opportunities; BSE will adapt and restrategize
items.quote: Every emerging regulatory and business environment is new, and therefore, the regulatory changes when they impact existing paradigm invokes a sense of concern at times. But what we need to notice, they also provide newer opportunities.

items.statement: Primary market capital raising INR 7.7 lakh crores via equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers
items.quote: BSE platforms continue to remind the preferred choice by Indian companies to raise capital by enabling issuers to raise INR 7.7 lakh crores by means of equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers, et cetera.

items.statement: StAR MF revenue up 101% YoY to INR 48 crores
items.quote: BSE StAR MF delivered yet another year of record revenues and performance, up 101% year-on-year to reach INR 48 crores.

items.statement: Clearing and settlement operational revenue up 40% to INR 33.8 crores
items.quote: The clearing and settlement operational revenues increased by 40% to INR 33.8 crores from INR 24.1 crores.

items.statement: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds up 179% to INR 62 crores
items.quote: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds has increased by 179% to INR 62 crores from INR 22.2 crores.

items.statement: Investment income up 43% to INR 62.9 crores
items.quote: Investment income increased by 43% to INR 62.9 crores from INR 44 crores.

items.statement: CloudTech expected to contribute 20-30% of total revenue
items.quote: But at the same time, if you look at the overall sector, we have CloudTech business between 20% to 30% of total revenue count.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 14.85% in Q1 FY25, up 329 bps QoQ
items.quote: Additionally, our EBITDA margin for Q1 FY25 stands at an impressive 14.85%, marking a substantial enhancement of 329 basis points from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Total addressable market over a trillion dollars growing at double-digit CAGR
items.quote: So, this total addressable market is over a trillion-dollar industry, okay. Considering that, there is lot of potential within India as well as in the international market.

items.statement: Six platforms across MadTech and CloudTech driving diversification
items.quote: So, under the umbrella, like I said, we have two major sub segments, MadTech and CloudTech. Definitely that's one side of the diversifications what we have built.

items.statement: Himalaya campaign reached 134 million audiences in 60 days
items.quote: The company spearhead a groundbreaking influencer campaign for Himalaya Turmeric Face Care range, reaching an impressive 134 million, that is 13.4 crore audiences with just 60 days averaging around 22 million per day.

items.statement: Happilo campaign on Zomato achieved over 100K coupon redemptions
items.quote: Vertoz also executed a highly successful campaign on Zomato for Happilo, a leading health food brand, resulting in over 100K coupons redemption.

items.statement: IncrementX partnered with Loop Media for CTV and DOOH monetization
items.quote: Moreover, Vertoz's IncrementX division partnered with Loop Media to elevate monetization for connected TV, CTV, digital out of home advertising.

items.statement: Investments primarily in intangible tech products and media platforms
items.quote: So being as a technology company, most of our investments are in the intangible, which is in tech products, intangible products, but consisting of the media properties and the platforms what we have built.

items.statement: Very minuscule debt, funded mainly through internal accruals
items.quote: There is a very minuscule amount of the debt. It's usually the accrued earnings what we have.

items.statement: Revenue grew 77.40% YoY to Rs 60.17 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our revenue for Q1 Financial Year '25 soared to Rs. 60.17 crore reflecting an exceptional growth of 77.40% year-on-year over year.

items.statement: PAT increased 61.94% YoY to Rs 5.74 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our profit after tax, PAT, for quarter one Financial Year '2025 reached Rs. 5.74 crore, representing a remarkable 61.94% year-over-year increase.

items.statement: Expanding US presence to capture larger market share
items.quote: Particularly, our expansion efforts in the United States have been significant, aiming to capture a large share of this crucial market and unlock new growth opportunities.

items.statement: Focus on self-improvement rather than external competitors
items.quote: So generally, we always believe that our biggest competition is we ourselves where we have to keep expanding our site.

items.statement: Thanked team for untiring efforts and hard work
items.quote: I thank the entire team of Vertoz for this untiring efforts, hard work, and dedication, digitized the company forward through the various market conditions.

items.statement: Management targets at least Rs 8,500 crore of sales for FY25.
items.quote: in this year we would be targeting a sale of at least about 8,500 crores and that's what we would continue to aim for.

items.statement: Management expects at least 6 million sq ft of launches in the remaining three quarters of FY25, taking full-year launches to about 9 million sq ft.
items.quote: remaining three quarters we should be able to do at least 6 million square feet. There is an upside potential to this definitely, but this is the number that we think we can surely do.

items.statement: Unsold inventory stands at 9.24 million sq ft; residential launch pipeline of 17.9 million sq ft across 16 projects in 7 cities to be launched over next six to eight quarters.
items.quote: currently we have 9.24 million square feet of unsold inventory. This gives us a great visibility for our teams to work on sales for the remaining years in addition to the planned launches for the next nine months.

items.statement: Future project pipeline from existing land bank and new deals estimated at 25-30 million sq ft, largely in Bangalore, with potential in Mumbai and Noida over 1.5-3 years.
items.quote: The current potential of these projects is about 30 million square feet. We will share the details of these projects as we move into forthcoming projects from time-to-time. The expected timeline to br ing these projects into launch stage is between one and a half to three

items.statement: Demand outlook steady across operating cities with supply catching up; NCR contributed 45.5% of Q1 sales value (Rs 852 cr) for the first time, overtaking Bangalore.
items.quote: The demand outlook in all our operating cities continues to be steady with supply catching up to the demand.

items.statement: Q1 saw highest-ever price realization due to shift toward high-ticket launches (>Rs 5 cr); remaining 18 million sq ft pipeline skewed to mid-income apartments of 1,800-2,000 sq ft.
items.quote: SOBHA's overall price realization in Q1 FY25 was the highest ever. This is because of the significant shift in our product mix aided by the recent launches.

items.statement: Project-level EBITDA margins on sales done in FY23, FY24 and Q1 FY25 exceed 30%; reported margins to improve steadily from next quarter and more meaningfully from FY26 as higher-margin revenue is recognized.
items.quote: our EBITDA margins at project level should be more than 30%. So, hence they will recover as we recognize these revenues in the coming years.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 44.5 cr incurred in Q1; Rs 161 cr invested in growth (likely land/development).
items.quote: We have invested in CAPEX close to 44.5 crores while higher due to start of construction of recently launched projects. During the quarter we have invested 161 crores in line with our growth focus.

items.statement: Quarterly collections hit record Rs 1,546 cr (real estate Rs 1,392 cr); net operating cash flow Rs 327 cr, up 68% YoY.
items.quote: Total collection from all the business amounted to Rs.1,546 crores in this quarter. Of this, about 1,392 crores were contributed by real estate businesses marking it the highest ever quarterly achievement as well as in our operating history.

items.statement: 15th consecutive quarter of net debt reduction; net debt down Rs 74 cr to ~Rs 1,200 cr; debt-equity 0.47x; post-rights net debt seen ~Rs 300 cr.
items.quote: These are 15 consecutive quarters of debt reduction. We reduced our net debt by 74 crores in the quarter and now our debt-equity is 0.47.

items.statement: Rights issue raised Rs 2,000 cr (1.21 mn shares at Rs 1,651, 1.39x subscribed); first tranche Rs 1,000 cr received; remaining tranches within 18 months.
items.quote: As you are aware, recently we have raised 2,000 crores through the capital market. We have issued 1.21 million shares at the rate Rs.1,651 per share and the rights issue was subscribed 1.39 times.

items.statement: GIFT City realizations risen from ~Rs 6,500 to ~Rs 10,000 over 4-5 years; new project launched at ~Rs 12,000/sq ft with strong traction.
items.quote: In the past four to five years particularly, we have seen an increase in the realization from earlier 6,500 to close to about 10,000. So, the new project that we launched is at about 12,000 and we are seeing decent traction.

items.statement: Completed 0.92 mn sq ft (564 units) in Q1; on track for ~5 mn sq ft deliveries in FY25 vs ~4 mn sq ft in FY24.
items.quote: we are on track to complete about 5 million square feet versus about 4 million square feet in the previous financial year.

items.statement: SOBHA share of forthcoming 18 mn sq ft pipeline estimated at 76-80%; JD partner share 20-24%.
items.quote: overall SOBHA share would be about in the range of 76% to 80%.

items.statement: RERA account restrictions limit cash extraction from owned-land projects, keeping gross debt ~Rs 2,000 cr despite strong collections.
items.quote: for owned land projects, it's far lower that we can take out. So, hence what number that you are seeing in terms of the cash that's lying in the books, that will be largely towards in the RERA accounts.

items.statement: Revenue recognition lagged in Q1 due to OC delays (partly election-related); expected to normalize from Q2 as OCs received post-quarter.
items.quote: delays in obtaining OCs have affected our revenue recognition and hence, going forward, the revenue recognition would be in a little lagged manner for the remainder of the financial year.

items.statement: Estimated margin cash flow from residential business Rs 16,200 cr (Rs 9,994 cr ongoing + Rs 6,210 cr forthcoming) for sales and marketing expense.
items.quote: we have an estimated margin cash flow of Rs.16,200 crores to be realized for sale s and marketing expense. Of this, Rs.9,994 crores is expected to come from our ongoing project s and balance 6,210 crores from our forthcoming projects

items.statement: Promoter holding increased ~0.5% in rights issue; no management changes mentioned.
items.quote: the promoters' share has gone up by about 0.5%.

items.statement: Contract revenue steady; management to de-emphasize civil contracts to focus resources on real estate and backward-integrated model.

items.statement: Oil & Gas segment trials progressing; long decision cycles but expecting developments in FY2025.

items.statement: Dr. Amit Prabhakar Pratap appointed as Additional Director; 20+ years expertise in oil, oleochemicals, surfactants.

Dr. Pratap is the Head of the Department at the Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai (formerly known as UDCT) and has covered over 20 years of expertise in oil, oleochemicals and Surfactants.

items.statement: Certified Great Place to Work for 3rd consecutive year in mid-size category.
items.quote: I am pleased to share that Fineotex has been certified as a great place to work in the mid-size organizations category for the 3rd consecutive year.

items.quote: Actually Bangladesh, we have an office also. We have a Company in Bangladesh. We have our team also. As such, Bangladesh is back to normal in terms of the production I am talking about. In terms of the factory running and other things and it is not right to assume that Bangladesh will be left behind because of these kinds of incidences which has happened. Of course it can take a little bit time to

items.quote: See what is again happening is there is a big shortage of the containers, freight charges. Again, the geopolitical situations are not okay. So, the shipping liners take a longer route. Longer route means less availability of the containers. At the same time, the cost is going up for that. So, these are the kinds of again, unpredictability, nobody will know how much inventory to keep in the pipelin

items.quote: So, it is not yet substantial at all. In fact, we are discussing with them to make it in a much better way, where we can really make the use of this tie up in a better way. As such, as you know, there has been again a problem with Europe because of the Red Sea issues and this and that and the Eurodye being located in Belgium, they are facing a hard time to make their products in Belgium Earnings C

items.statement: Continuous new product development driven by end-user sustainability demands; new products added monthly.
items.quote: There are so many products going on day in and day out. Because in this business where we are, there is always a new trend coming up. There is always a new demand from the end user. Let us say Walmarts of the world. They will always keep sharing their challenges or something which they want us to achieve for. So, we always keep getting our challenges and we keep working towards it in order to get

items.statement: Aggressively developing outdoor lighting (landscape, facade) and home segment (decorative, semi-decorative technical lighting) with worldwide patent on technology; also targeting trade segment with screw-less, fast-assembly products
items.quote: Currently we are working very aggressively on outdoor profile. Outdoor is a very huge market till India is concerned and India, Middle East and Europe is concerned. And we are working on landscape and we are working on facade lighting, building facades.

items.statement: Introduced technical lighting in home segment, now expanding into decorative and semi-decorative technical lighting for stronger foothold
items.quote: In home segment, we are working very, very aggressively. We introduced technical lighting. Now we are going in a segment of decorative lighting and semi -decorative technical lighting, which gives us a very, very strong foothold in home segment.

items.statement: Entering trade segment with differentiated screw-less products, exclusive designs, and fast assembly (10-25 seconds) to reduce cost and create differentiation in price-sensitive market
items.quote: We are working on a very different level wherein we are introducing products which are screw-less. We are introducing products with very different materials, unlike what is used in trade. We are introducing a lot of exclusive designs and technology in trade.

items.statement: Debt increased significantly; receivables from Middle East and Southeast Asia channel partners delayed but assured to be cleared by September-October; INR6 crores already collected in home lighting
items.quote: Yes, the debt has gone very high. We are working with a few channel partners, especially in the Middle East and in Southeast Asia. Now with channel partners, when it comes to home segment, we are not doing direct business in Middle East and in Southeast Asia.

items.statement: CFO confirms INR6 crores collected towards home lighting vs previous quarter; retail lighting collections also being followed aggressively; most over-6-month receivables expected by September-October end
items.quote: So if you see, as compared to previous quarter, we have collected almost INR6 crores towards the home lighting. And in retail lighting also, we are following up very aggressively. So by September or October end, we will be able to receive most of the amount, which is above six months.

items.statement: Currently managing working capital without problems; may face stress once outdoor portfolio launches and might need to raise limits
items.quote: Till date, we still don't have problems and we are surviving and we are able to manage it. Once the outdoor portfolio is done, we might have a stress and we might have to raise or increase our limits.

items.statement: Dividend policy to be announced; dividend expected to be declared at next meeting
items.quote: Dividend here, we will announce. Of course, we will come out with the dividend policy and we will give the dividend. I think next meeting we will announce the dividend for sure.

items.statement: Domestic home segment routed through 30-35 channel partners (target 50); each partner potential INR1-5 crores annually; experience centers in Andheri, factory, Bangalore, Lower Parel, with Delhi and Pune finalized; partner centers in Hydera
items.quote: All put together, we have 35 channel partners right now. Between 30 to 35, I don't know the exact numbers. And this year we are planning to increase it to 50 channel partners. Till date, average channel partner's potential with us was somewhere between 50 lakhs to 1 crore. Their potential can increase up to 5 crores in local, I am talking about India.

items.statement: Middle East home channel: tie-ups with three companies; one opened experience center in Saudi Arabia last month, second planned in Dubai; Saudi market growing significantly
items.quote: Till Middle East is concerned, we have tie up with three companies. And one of the companies have been very keen and they have opened experience center in Saudi. It has just opened last month. And Saudi, the way India is growing, Saudi is growing in a very big way.

items.statement: No railway orders secured this quarter; railway tendering system in turmoil with quality concerns and vendor due diligence; approved vendor status achieved with private players (Bombardier, Alstom) but factory visits and traction taking tim
items.quote: No, railway currently we are not able to secure any orders. Railway, there are two systems where railway works. One is there are private players, companies like Bombardier or Alstom who buys lights and who installs in the boogies and supplies it to railway.

items.statement: Airport orders: Mumbai Airport INR7-8 crores (Phase 1 of 4 phases, full completion expected by Dec/Feb); Guwahati Airport Phase 1 received; Indore Airport order received; approved by Airport Authority of India; working closely with Adani (2
items.quote: Guwahati was received before Mumbai. Both are phase 1. This is not a complete order. Okay. We have received in Mumbai there are 4 phases. And this is the first order what we have received. The government of India is supposed to complete it by this. They were supposed to complete it by August. But I don't think so it is happening for them. So probably by December or by Feb.

items.statement: Government projects: working with Ahmedabad Tourism (large inquiries concluding next month), Surat Municipal Corporation (designing street light, conclusion in 6 months), Central Vista/Secretariat orders via L&T; government share increasing
items.quote: We are working with Ahmedabad Tourism in a very big way. There are some huge inquiries and they should be concluded by next month. We are expecting. It is a very large value for a company like us. We are working very closely with Surat SMC, Municipal Corporation.

items.statement: Confident on sustaining top-line growth and expanded margins over 3-5 year horizon across four verticals (trade, outdoor, home, retail) with patents and technology investments; visibility good for 2-3 years; acknowledges possible 1-2 quarte
items.quote: As a company, what we are looking at is three years and five years bandwidth. Okay. The investments what currently we are doing in three major verticals. And we've got patents and we are working on different technologies in trade, in outdoor and in home. And of course, retail also.

items.statement: Home segment revenue cyclical (spikes with large builder projects); Q1 home revenue declined from INR6 crores to INR2 crores due to project timing; not a benchmark; similar lumpiness expected in infra segment
items.quote: See, you have to understand. There is a builder. I will just give you an example. Loda or DLS is coming out with a township. And you get the order. Then you will see a spike in one quarter. Which is a very normal thing. But it is not that DLS completed one project and he will come out with immediately a second project.

items.statement: Stock price decline (150 to 86-87 over two months) attributed to profit booking by long-term investors; management focused on business growth, not daily stock tracking
items.quote: No, it is you, investors. I should at this is one question which I have to ask rather than you asking me. Sorry, this is not my job to track day to day what is happening. Of course, it is. We are growing and we were expecting the market to react positively. But I think people are encashing profit and there are investors in the company for a very long time.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant under construction with three tube mills, slitting line, galvanizing unit; 10,000 tonnes capacity similar to Maharashtra plant
items.quote: At the moment, after the land being purchased, the plant is under process. We have erected two tube mills, three tube mills we are installing in that area with Slitting line and galvanized unit.

items.statement: Hyderabad added second galvanizing line for crash barrier production; achieved 1,200 tonnes dispatch last month vs 500 tonnes earlier
items.quote: Just last month, we have achieved the target of 1200 tonnes of dispatch of galvanized product called crash barrier or highway guardrail, before that it is used to be only 500 tonnes.

items.statement: Orders placed for Octagon Pole and High Mast Pole machinery to be installed at Jharsuguda
items.quote: we are in way of achieving the machineries for those products are also being placed, orders of those machines have been placed and they shall also be getting installed in Jharsuguda location in its view.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant trial run or production targeted for Q2 FY25
items.quote: we had given a timeline of somewhere 2nd Quarter and 2nd Quarter for the plant to start its trial run or its production and we are well on our way to achieve that target.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant production expected by September or October 2024; GI plant ~50% complete; one month delay due to heavy rain
items.quote: I feel we are going to be in the production in the month of September, it may go up to October, but not beyond that.

items.statement: Monopole machinery delivery expected August or September 2024
items.quote: The machineries like monopole and all will be finalized, and that machine will come in the month of August or September, I think so.

items.statement: Expect increase in production, sales, and profit visible in October-November 2024
items.quote: All these things are happening now which you can watch very easily in the month of October and November, you can watch increase in production, increase in sales, and increase in profit.

items.statement: Profit decline due to steel price correction post-COVID; prices back to pre-COVID levels; volume stable
items.quote: This decline of the profit is a cycle of steel which was expected after the revise of steel prices due to covid. The ripple effect of covid has taken its own due course to settle up.

items.statement: Quantity sold Q1 FY25 36,747 tonnes vs 38,129 tonnes Q4 FY24; revenue impact from price decline not volume
items.quote: Last quarter in 2023-24, the quantity was 38,129 and 2024-25, it is 36,747, so quantity wise it is not decreased, because of the pricing goes down, that's why sale is effected in the terms of amount.

items.statement: IPO proceeds (Rs 72.17 cr) mostly used for raw material procurement; ~Rs 3 cr remaining in FD
items.quote: This working capital is only utilized in our procurement of raw material which was the reason why we raised IPO. It was mentioned as well and that's exactly were the fund has been utilized. Most of the fund is utilized there. I think we have very little, which is in the form of FD. I am not sure about the exact number it should be around 3 crores.

items.statement: IPO funds reduced working capital debt; CC/OD interest cost under control; interest expense to decrease significantly
items.quote: I believe with the IPO being successful, the money has been raised for working capital. So, now we have been able to manage our debt significantly effectively so that has been taken care and so our bank interest for the working capital which is a CC or OD limit that has been under control which was our target.

items.statement: Long-term assets funded via internal accruals and term loans, not IPO proceeds
items.quote: No not for the long-term assets. It has been done through our internal approval and also the term loan that we had taken from the bank.

items.statement: Total installed capacity 221,000 metric tonnes per annum across two units each in Telangana and Maharashtra
items.quote: VSTL has two manufacturing units each in Telangana and Maharashtra with the total installed capacity of 221,000 metric tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant capacity 10,000 tonnes similar to Maharashtra plant
items.quote: The installed capacity of Jharsuguda plant is similar to what we have in the western region of India in Maharashtra, which are 10,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Crash barrier (highway guardrail) production ramped up; new products Octagon Pole and High Mast Pole planned for Jharsuguda
items.quote: during IPO, we had promised that once we established ourselves in crash barriers, we will go ahead and introduce other products as well such as Octagon Pole, High Mast Pole and we are in way of achieving the machineries for those products are also being placed

items.statement: IPO in February 2024 raised Rs 72.17 crores on BSE and NSE
items.quote: in February 2024, VSTL made a stellar debut on BSE and NSE raising Rs. 72.17 crores from the IPO.

items.statement: Stock placed under SEBI surveillance; management attributes price decline to surveillance
items.quote: Because they have put this share in surveillance, SEBI has put this share in surveillance that's why it is down.

items.statement: Jharsuguda project faced labor shortage during elections and heavy rain delays
items.quote: Two months later, elections came up, and since the laborers were from Bihar, they couldn't come. Then it rained for two months. Despite all these challenges, we continued to work with full determination.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target for FY25 is Rs.675-700 crores with 25-30% growth over last year
items.quote: we are still on line to achieve Rs.675-700 crores consolidated revenue with a growth of at least Jash Engineering Limited 25-30% over last year

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve to 13-13.5% in FY25 from 12-12.5% last year
items.quote: We expect to improve our margins of last year . Last year, we had around 12 -125% PAT margin and we expect to improve it to 13-1305% this year

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at Rs.939 crores including 80% of Waterfront's Rs.26 crores orders
items.quote: Our consolidated order book position as of now is Rs.939 crores. And in this we have also considered 80% of Rs.26 crores total order booking for Waterfront

items.statement: July order bookings reached Rs.107 crores (Rs.59 crores export, Rs.38 crores domestic), one of the highest monthly bookings
items.quote: in the month of July we were able to book orders, when I say book order this were registered in our books and have arrived in the company worth Rs.107 crores of which around Rs.59 crores were for projects outside India and Rs.38 crores was for projects in India

items.statement: Rs.60 crores negotiated in July expected in August, plus Rs.43 crores under negotiation
items.quote: We have already negotiated in the month of July for Rs.60 crores which we expect to receive within August. And various orders worth for Rs.43 crores is under negotiation

items.statement: Rs.29 crores planned for FY25 across facilities; Chennai plant (60,000 sq ft, Rs.20 crores) ready by year-end; Indore SEZ plant (64,000 sq ft, Rs.23 crores) commissioning by end of next year
items.quote: In this financial year we are planning to invest around Rs.29 crores in our various facility shown here. Once this investment is done it will significantly add to our output as well as profitability

items.statement: Current facility supports Rs.800 crores turnover potential; targeting Rs.1,000 crores capacity by end of next year with new plants adding Rs.100 crores each
items.quote: The current facility which we have is doing a turnover potential of close Rs.800 crores. We are adding to it so that in year or so we reach Rs.1000 crores capacity

items.statement: Consolidated PAT turned positive in Q1 FY25 for first time; PAT margin improved from -5.1% to breakeven
items.quote: As you can see, our PAT margin in Q1FY24 was -5.1% it has now come to zero which shows that this quarter we had significant improvement

items.statement: Rodney Hunt legacy orders ($5-6M of $47M order book) impacting margins; impact to reduce as revenue scales to $35-39M annually
items.quote: The legacy orders Jash Engineering Limited are worth $5-6 million out of the order book of $47 million. So, as every quarter execution increases the deformation of legacy order on the profitability will reduce

items.statement: Strong opportunities from wastewater reuse, desalination, storm water, flood prevention and rising sea levels globally
items.quote: I would like to highlight that the company is facing good opportunities from new business which are reused waste water, desalination, storm water, flood situation and rising sea levels

items.statement: Hong Kong order of Rs.34 crores received in July for flood prevention and rising sea level project
items.quote: one of the large orders which we received last month in July from Hongkong which was worth Rs.34 crores which is a project for flood prevention and rising sea level

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue split: Rs.76 crores export (67%) vs Rs.39 crores domestic (33%); US order book at $47M
items.quote: in the first quarter we had a revenue of Rs.114 crores out of which Rs.76 crores was outside India and Rs.39 crores in India

items.statement: Q1 revenue mix: Water control gates 49%, Screens 30%, Balance equipment 7% (varies ±5%)
items.quote: Water control gates is our biggest product group and it contribute 49% to our revenue in Q1, Screen was the second group which contributed 30% and all balance equipment contributed 7%

items.statement: MCGM project: 90% gate market share across 6 of 7-8 projects; screens ~90%, valves starting
items.quote: out of 7-8 projects, 90% of companies have led with Jash

items.statement: Thailand market recovering post-elections; $2M+ orders received, expecting $3-4M this year
items.quote: we have received already now orders worth more than $2 million. This year we expect to receive total orders worth $3-4 million from Thailand alone

items.statement: US screen re-entry planned: team hiring by year-end, then approvals and marketing; Mahr brand advantage
items.quote: Our plan is by the end of this year to start putting people in place first and then going for approval as well as for marketing of the product

items.statement: Indian government announced flood protection and 100-city water/wastewater schemes; tendering process takes ~1 year, business from next year
items.quote: the government has announced two scheme to elevate protection. And also, investment in 100 cities. In infrastructure of water wastewater. So, these are just announced, by the time this will come on paper and on the ground, it will be sometime next year

items.statement: Rodney Hunt performance bond requirements easing: banks reduced margin from 45-50% to 30%, targeting 10-15% in a year
items.quote: the banks are willing to go down from 45-50% which they were asking us to deposit us as value for performance bond, the bank is now willing to consider 30%

items.statement: Waterfront acquired 2 months ago for UK water business; sent India-trained manager to apply Rodney Hunt lessons
items.quote: Waterfront was acquired very recently two months back to focus on the UK water business which has huge potential

items.statement: Share split approved: Rs.10 face value to five Rs.2 shares; direct listing on BSE planned alongside NSE
items.quote: we have decided to split the share of Rs.10 into five shares of Rs.2 each as well as go for direct listing of shares on Bombay Stock Exchange

items.statement: Water treatment plant: 75% civil, 25% electrotechnical (5-10% addressable); Wastewater: 65% civil, 35% electrotechnical (5-10% addressable)
items.quote: In water treatment plan t 75% would be civil and 25% would be electrotechnical equipment. However, in wastewater treatment plant 65% will be civil and 35% electrotechnical equipment. In 35% electrotechnical equipment our contribution, if we get all the job would be anywhere between 5-10%

items.statement: Large US project ($25-30M) may be declined if client insists on full US manufacturing; current US capacity limited to $12M order book
items.quote: The other big job in America is in trouble now because they want us to manufacture it in America, and it is such a big job there to take it for manufacturing in America may become very risky

items.statement: Invent JV progressing slowly due to strategic differences; German partner prefers high margins over volumes; 6-12 month evaluation timeline
items.quote: we got a feeling that Invent was not willing to move aggressively . It i s a German company which is more interested on high profits rather than high volumes

items.statement: Promoter family selling 2% stake (SEBI approved) for personal reasons; family retains 42-43%, combined with Axel Schutte >50%
items.quote: Patel family have taken permission to from SEBI as well as NSE to sell 2% of the stake. This was taken 2 years back and slowly we are selling 2% of our stake despite of selling all these stakes on an average our family stake is still more than 42-43%

items.statement: Completed INR200 crore QIP, first capital raise in ~30 years, institutional holding up from ~5% to 10.6%
items.quote: And the second point, friends, is that -- which is again historical, is that we have successfully completed our QIP. It was long overdue. And this is, again, historic in a sense that this is a capital event in the company almost after 30 years.

items.statement: INR123 crore (61% of QIP) allocated for capex: INR78 crore for API capacity 400KL to 600KL, INR40-43 crore for medical devices capacity expansion
items.quote: As, Purva, you may already might have seen in the presentation, so 61% of the money, around INR123 crores, is being used for the capex and out of which around INR75 crores is for the -- INR78 crores is for the APIs, for the increasing capacities of the APIs, from 400 KL to 600

items.statement: Medical devices capacity expansion: glucometers 2.5M to 5M, strips 500M to 700M, BP monitors 1.2M to 2.5M; API capacity 400KL to 600KL; full operation within 12-18 months
items.quote: And within 18 to 12 months, all the capacities will be full operation.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 15-20% CAGR; blended EBITDA margin improvement 3-4% over 2-3 years from current ~12% to ~15%
items.quote: From a financial impact point of view, so the new capacities will help us achieve the EBITDA margins and -- a little higher EBITDA margins, 3% to 4%, and of course, to achieve a revenue growth of 15% to 20%, which we have been doing earlier.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 blended EBITDA margin 12% (up from 7% YoY); pharma EBITDA margin target ~10.5% for FY25, devices ~15%
items.quote: So after a very long time, in the first quarter , we have got a two -digit -- double-digit EBITDA margins, which is 93% up.

items.statement: Medical devices industry growing 15-20% CAGR; India market $11B to $50B by 2030; company growing at 25-27% CAGR in devices
items.quote: As per the government estimate, it is going to be $50 billion in 2030, which is like we are seeing that is seven, eight years away. So the market of medical devices is growing 15%, 20% CAGR year -on-year.

items.statement: 12.3 million glucometers installed base; sold 12 crore strips in Q1 (25-30% growth); BP monitors 29% growth in Q1
items.quote: We have 12 million -- 12.3 million meters installed in the market. That's like our customer base. So typically, they say that, okay, whatever the customer is there, so he would keep on buying the strips regularly.

items.statement: Medical devices revenue share increased from 26% to 30.2%; API exports 71% of pharma revenue; 6 core API products contribute 85% of API revenue
items.quote: And this year, this quarter, the medical device share has gone up more than 30%. So 30.2% is the medical devices business.

items.statement: Raw material price softening from China post-COVID improved gross margins; backward integration in devices to reduce import dependence
items.quote: And due to softening of the prices also, the raw material prices, our gross margins have also increased.

items.statement: API exports grew 31% YoY; Europe up 130%, South America 80%, Asia Pacific strong; US down 33% due to high base; India API sales down 16%
items.quote: And interesting point here is 31% increase in the export business. So export, of course, is primarily for the API business. So there's a 31% increase.

items.statement: Devices working capital ~70 days, API ~90+ days; devices historically negative working capital (advance payments) but increasing due to backward integration
items.quote: For API, it was 90 days -plus. So I think we should be able to maintain these numbers as we go further. Maybe in devices, because we are doing backward integration, the working capital will go up as we do more in-house manufacturing.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; QIP proceeds used for capex and working capital, not debt repayment
items.quote: Though we are a debt-free company, but we were shy of raising fresh debt, but long-term capital was required in the

items.statement: API: 700+ customers (500 global, 200 India); Devices: 128,000 retail outlets targeting 300,000 in 3 years; Walmart, Walgreens, CVS auditing facilities
items.quote: We have more than 700 customers, out of which 500 customers are located worldwide, in all the U.S. The advanced market like U.S., Europe, Taiwan, Korea, Japan.

items.statement: Roche reportedly folding sales team into diabetic division (media reports); Dr. Morepen gaining market share; KBC advertising with Amitabh Bachchan
items.quote: Roche has upfolded its sales team into their diabetic team. It's the media news. And certainly, they are in an attempt to only focus on the distribution of the strips and meters to a distributor.

items.statement: Government of India promoting medical devices manufacturing; QR code/hologram guidelines for anti-counterfeit; PLI scheme context
items.quote: Government of India is now coming with a guideline that, okay, you can scan it and check with your QR code.

items.statement: API asset turnover 7.2x (target improvement); Devices asset turnover ~10.5x (stabilizing to 8.5-9x with backward integration)
items.quote: So asset turnover for API, we have 7.2. So we shall be able to maintain this asset turnover. In the future, maybe we'll improve our asset turnover.

items.statement: China price volatility risk; counterfeit products on e-commerce; US market demand softness; execution risk on capacity expansion timeline
items.quote: So now the position of China is that they are sitting on full warehouses, fully-stacked warehouses and there are no customers to buy because the demand was not so much as was at the time of pressure in COVID.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focused on R&D and backward integration capabilities
items.quote: We have to have service, we have to have relationships and we have to have backward integration, we have to have cost saving, and more importantly, any technology of development

items.statement: Jammu Greenfield project expected turnover-to-investment ratio of 1.25-1.3x
items.quote: the turnover to investment ratio is anything between 1.25 to 1.3X.

items.statement: Board approved ~₹740 crore Greenfield unit in Jammu for recycled PET chips and filament yarn
items.quote: At the board meeting held on 9th Augus t 2024, the board approved a capital expenditure of approximately ₹740 crores to establish a Greenfield unit in

items.statement: Jammu project plant & machinery investment ~₹400 crore eligible for 3x subsidy over 10 years capped at GST
items.quote: Out of 700 Cr, 400 something let's say in plant and machinery, the subsidy will be 400*3 = 1200 Cr over the period of 10 years, which is 120 Cr every year

items.statement: No other substantial capex plans beyond Jammu project
items.quote: Other than that, as of now we do not have any other plan going for substantially you can say capital expenditure.

items.statement: Jammu Greenfield unit to produce 270 metric tons per day of recycled PET chips and filament yarn
items.quote: This new facility will produce recycled pet chips and recycled filament yarn with an expected production capacity of 270 metric tons per day.

items.statement: Knitting facility currently 600 tons per month, another 100 tons to be operational by end of calendar year
items.quote: Knitting like in 16 months, we have c ome up with a facility of 600 tons per mont h, which is a very sizable commodity, you know, so going forward probably after 18 or 24 months we can think of adding something

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin improved 155 bps QoQ to 35.9%, EBITDA margin declined 17 bps QoQ
items.quote: Also, the gross profit margin improved by 155 basis points quarter over quarter to 35.9% although there was a slight decrease of 135 basis points on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin recovery to 10% depends on geopolitical normalization (Ukraine-Russia, Middle East, Red Sea)
items.quote: A lot depends actually, you know what the geopolitical situation takes shape, you know, for the last two years, company like RSWM which was having 35% in export volume and many companies, you know, which were having substantial, you can say export exposure, they got impacted first due to Ukraine-Russia war and off late you know due to what is happening in the Middle East.

items.statement: Domestic polyester prices 17-18% above international due to QCO, China dumping yarn made from cheaper polyester

items.statement: Huron Q1 FY25 order inflow ~Rs 97 crore; all aerospace & defense orders currently from Huron; domestic defense orders to start in FY25
items.quote: So, basically even in Q1, we have received close to 97 crores. Let's say we have dispatches like that for close to 153 crores. But we have received the orders are close to 97 crores, and we are anticipating in that entity and to combine duty together, because the customers are common.

items.statement: EMS customer qualification completed; ~Rs 100 crore machines to dispatch in Q2, rest in Q3; new EMS orders expected in Q2, large orders in Q3
items.quote: So, this quarter, out of this, our pending order from EMS, close to 100 crore machine will dispatch into a 2nd Quarter, and rest of the machines are going to be dispatched in the 3rd Quarter. This is how our total position is and based on another area that we already discussed last year, we are developing many new product to match our aerospace, as well as to the EMS sectors.

items.statement: Smartphone ecosystem localization driving machine demand; >1 lakh machines needed over 7-8 years across various operations

items.statement: Year-end FY25 order book target minimum INR200 crores plus

items.quote: But if I look at it from a balance sheet point of view, we should have 10% to 20% of our hybrid or our theme park EPC business should get capitalized this year plus the Noida projects which should get capitalized at another INR10 to INR15 crores.

items.statement: 7-8 new theme parks expected to go live by March 2025
items.quote: Between now and let's say March, we expect a minimum of seven, eight parks probably going online, if not more.

items.statement: 20+ projects in tender pipeline, expect to win majority by December 2024
items.quote: So, we have almost around 20-odd projects where the tenders are either floated or the tenders are in the process of coming out. And we expect to win majority of them within next probably by end of December.

items.statement: Blue-chip wastewater clients: Grasim, Gujarat Alkalies, Navin Fluorine, DCM Shriram; theme park clients are municipal corporations/development authorities
items.quote: So, as we speak, you know, we have blue chip customers like Grasim, Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals, Navin Fluorine, DCM Shriram, very, very discerning, and demanding customers where we have executed these projects.

items.statement: Theme park model: government funds 80-90% capex, Z-Tech puts 10-20%; EPC margin on govt portion, revenue share on own portion
items.quote: First of all, in all our hybrid projects, we don't like to or neither we want to put more than 10 to 20 percent of the total cost of the project. So, let's say the project is worth INR10 crores, and my cost of that project is INR6 crores. So, the government is giving me INR8 crores. So, I am making an EPC margin of INR2 crores. And I am leaving, the INR2 crores of my further margin getting as a pa

items.statement: Theme park revenue streams: ticketing, F&B rental+rev share, kids activities, adventure, retail, events, branding/advertising
items.quote: The sources of revenue, the first source of revenue is the EPC. The second source of the revenue is ticket share. The third source of the revenue is in F&B rental plus revenue share. The fourth is the kids activities. Fifth is the adventure activities. Sixth is the retail area. Seventh is the events. Eighth is the branding advertisement. These are the ones at least we are clear about.

items.quote: charge a fixed rental plus a 15% revenue share. The entire investment is theirs. So, we make money on two counts. Sunil Ghorawat: Ticketing revenue comes to us and then we give the government their

items.statement: No funding challenge for next year; businesses are profitable and cash-generating
items.quote: We have funding for the next year. Because our businesses are profitable enough that they are cash generating too. So, we don't see that as a challenge.

items.statement: IPO raised INR37.30 crores via 33.91 lakh new shares; oversubscribed 371x; listed June 5, 2024 on LSE FME platform
items.quote: One of our key achievements is our IPO listing on June 5, 2024. This journey began with filing our DRHP, followed by the RHP, and culminated in a successful IPO that was oversubscribed by more than 371 times. We raised 37.30 crores through the issuance of 33.91 lakh new shares.

items.statement: Government initiatives supporting metal recycling: Metal Recycling Policy, Swachh Bharat, Make in India; water sector: AMRUT, Namami Gange, Community Drinking Water Scheme
items.quote: has recognized the importance of metal scrap recycling and has taken several steps to support and encourage the industry. Initiatives such as Metal Recycling Policy, the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and Make in India have created a favourable environment for the recycling sector to thrive. items.statement: International expansion discussions ongoing; team to be built in H2 FY25; targeting higher realization; dialogues with External Affairs Ministry and Tourism Ministry

Part of our strategy is also to probably work with the Indian External Affairs Ministry to create this more as a friendship path. So, we have also started the dialogue with the External Affairs Ministry. Similarly, like the Ministry of Tourism.

items.statement: Execution risks: weather (rains/floods in H1), site conditions, manpower, waste material sourcing for theme parks
items.quote: Sir, major challenges, number one is nature, number two is site conditions, number three is manpower. Very conventional challenges which any project execution faces. There is nothing very unique about it, except, in theme parks sometimes we have to struggle for the kind of waste material, which is required, and a corporation or authority might not have it.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 50-60% (INR225 crores revenue, INR40 crores PAT suggested by analyst; management confident)
items.quote: We intend to, and we are very confident about it.

items.statement: Management will wait another quarter to give proper volume growth guidance; growth expected to be slightly lower than earlier targets
items.quote: It will definitely be better than Q1, but still because of global uncertainties, demand in US and Europe is still subdued. So, we haven't been able to get a clear picture of how much we will be Gateway Distriparks Limited & growing. So, we will wait maybe another quarter to give proper guidance, but it is slightly lower than what we were targeting

items.statement: Management targets double-digit volume growth but cannot give specific guidance due to macro uncertainties
items.quote: We will definitely be looking in double digit, but it all depends on the macros.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA per TEU at Rs 9,400; margin slipped due to lower volumes and double stack percentage dropping 2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has slipped a little bit because of the low volumes and our double stack percentage has gone down by say 2% this quarter so that reflects on the EBITDA margin

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU improved to Rs 1,350-1,375 from Rs 520 last quarter
items.quote: CFS has maintained the same volume. And I mean the margins on CFS, if you compare them from the last quarter, which was from three digits have gone up to Rs.1,350 - Rs.1,375, last quarter it was Rs.520 only.

items.statement: Double stacking dropped from 39% average last year to 33% in Q1; recovery to 40%+ would directly improve EBITDA
items.quote: So, last year we averaged at about 39%, but this quarter, we were at 33%. As and when the volume cut back and the imbalance within the ports also like Mundra, Pipavav, JNPT our volumes, some were import-heavy, some were export-heavy. Once this number comes back to say 40% which we have done in the past, we have even gone up to 45% in the past it will just straight away add to the EBITDA and the bo

items.statement: Red Sea impact and port congestion continue; slight improvement seen in June-July but US/Europe demand remains subdued
items.quote: Overall that red sea impact still continues, there has been a lot of port congestion at various international ports, vessel schedule has been erratic over the last few months. But slightly we have seen some improvement in June, July is also looking slightly better.

items.statement: Wastepaper imports down 30% at Kashipur and 10% at Ludhiana; bookings improving in July-August
items.value: 30% drop at Kashipur, 10% drop at Ludhiana
items.quote: Kashipur, 85% of the wastepaper is import. So, there has been close to 30% drop in Kashipur. And in Ludhiana we have 20% of our import volumes and there has been almost 10% drop in the import waste paper.

items.statement: Market share in NCR marginally up from ~16% to ~17%; Ludhiana down YoY from 28% to 22.5% but up from Q4; Uttarakhand at ~25%
items.quote: NCR, we have marginally gone up from, say, 16 -point something to almost 17% in Ludhiana, on a YoY basis we have gone down from 28% to 22.5%, but even Q1 is higher than Q4 last year. So, Ludhiana, we started gaining back a little bit of market share and that should improve going forward. Uttarakhand is at about 25% and this fluctuates plus/minus 2% every quarter because the market itself is small.

items.statement: Jaipur terminal expected operational in ~12 months; litigation ongoing but backup plan exists
items.quote: According to our present estimates, we will be operational in about 12 months from now.

items.statement: New ICD planned in North India; land identified but not yet acquired; will be full-fledged ICD with double stacking
items.quote: It will be in north of India. So, it is yet to crystallize, I mean we have identified the land and once we have a deal and we acquire the land that will be the appropr iate time to inform the location

items.statement: Faridabad double stacking work expedited by Indian Railways; expected operational in couple of months
items.quote: They have assured us that they are going to expedite the work and plus due to election also there was some kind of delay, but now Indian Railways has assured us that they have sent a special team and now the work has started in full swing. So, we are expecting that in another couple of months, soon it will be operational.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to stay at 6-7% for next two years
items.quote: Yes, it will stay like this for the next two years at least.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 245 crores, down significantly from Rs 800 crores peak; gross debt Rs 310 crores
items.quote: Our debt situation is very good right now. I mean we at our lowest net debt to Rs. 245 crores compared to which was at one time Rs. 800 crores or something and even from last quarter last year, if you see it has come down significantly.

items.statement: CFS monetization under evaluation; preparing information memorandum; Nhava Sheva property expected to fetch good valuation
items.quote: We are in the process of putting down everything on paper and preparing information memorandum for any potential buyer to look into.

items.statement: GDL stake in Snowman at 46.4%; can acquire up to 5% per year under creeping acquisition; may exceed 50% by year-end if full 5% acquired
items.quote: See, we are allowed to acquire 5% under creeping acquisition rules. So, last year we acquired 5%, this year we have acquired a little over 1% and we are at 46.4% now and if we complete the full 5% acquisition in this financial year, so we should be ending up little over 50%.

items.statement: Snowman 5PL (distribute) business targets 25%+ YoY growth; grew 29% QoQ and 12% YoY in Q1
items.quote: We have expectations of more than 25% YoY growth on this particular vertical to distribute which is the 5PL vertical. As you see, we have grown 29% over the last quarter and 12% over last year same quarter.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing business expects 12-15% growth in FY25 with new facilities in Lucknow and Kolkata
items.quote: Considering the new facilities which are going to be functional in next month, Lucknow and after that Kolkata, and also some of the lease capacities which we are yet to fully utilize, considering all these, we expect around 12% to 15% growth in warehousing business this year.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing realization up 2.5% YoY; expects another 1% increase next quarter
items.quote: Also, warehousing realization has gone up by 2.5% as compared to last year and we expect it to go by another 1% in the next quarter because some of the price corrections have happened now, which will start yielding in the coming quarter.

items.statement: New 5PL client from ice cream/dairy industry signed; expected to contribute Rs 15-18 crores/quarter from Q2
items.quote: It is from ice cream and dairy industry, and this is expected to contribute anywhere between 15 to 18 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Rail busy season surcharge of 10% passed on to customers; hope for revision to improve competitiveness vs road
items.quote: So, little bit, road does have an advantage with the 10% busy season surcharge that came in. Although we passed it on, we had no choice but to pass i t on to our customers and that's been fully implemented now. But maybe hopefully this can be revised in the near future and then can get a better pricing to make it more competitive

items.statement: DFC Western corridor 93% complete; last 100 km to Vaitarna will take time; commissioning guidance December 2025
items.quote: DFC is giving us guidance for December 2025. And again, the status is the same that 93% of the total WDFC has completed up to Vaitarna and the last leg of 100 kilometers is still going to take a lot of time.

items.statement: EXIM imbalance persists at port level (Mundra imports down, Pipavav imports up) affecting double stacking despite overall 52:48 import:export ratio
items.quote: Yes, but then if you look at within the ports what used to be there like Mundra imports have gone down, Pipavav imports have gone up, so within that there is imbalance. So, for a train running perspective, it is still an imbalance in certain markets.

items.statement: CFS business faces intense competition with no players exiting; management wants to exit but not in a hurry
items.quote: we would definitely want to get out of the CFS business because even though the margins have increased in the first quarter compared to last q uarter of the year, but at the same time, we don't see any uptick on the CFS business because the competition is so intense and there is hardly anyone who has moved out of this business

items.statement: Accounting policy change: consolidator discounts now netted from revenue (Rs 8.43 cr impact); no impact on EBITDA per TEU
items.quote: This is basically a business model done with consolidators, but it was discount being passed on was actually earlier being counted in the revenue. But as per the accounting standard now, that comes under gross revenue, but under net revenue we have to remove this discount. So, it was like a pass-through almost. So, it's gone away from this quarter on.

name: The New India Assurance Company Limited

items.statement: Target double-digit ROE in short to medium term (1-3 years)
